ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a single-phase full-bridge voltage-source inverter circuit, with the DC power supply on the left labeled as 200 V, a pure inductive load connected between the midpoints of the bridge arms, the inductor labeled as 0.1 H, and the load current direction marked as i0. Reasoning: The problem statement gives the inverter frequency f = 50 Hz and adopts the 180° square-wave operating mode. For a full-bridge 180° square wave, the voltage across the inductor is +Vdc = +200 V in one half-cycle and -200 V in the next half-cycle. The period T = 1/f = 1/50 = 0.02 s, so the half-period T/2 = 0.01 s. The change in inductor current within a half-cycle is Δi = (V/L)(T/2) = (200/0.1)(0.01) = 20 A. Also because the problem states that the load current has no DC component, the current waveform is symmetric about zero, changing linearly from -Ipk to +Ipk within a half-cycle, so 2Ipk = 20 A, giving Ipk = 10.0 A.

method.method_draft: From the image take Vdc = 200 V and L = 0.1 H. From the text take f = 50 Hz and 180° square-wave operation. In a full bridge, vL is +200 V for one half-period and -200 V for the next. The half-period is T/2 = 1/(2f) = 0.01 s. Compute current change in one half-cycle: Δi = (Vdc/L)(T/2) = (200/0.1)(0.01) = 20 A. Since the current has no DC component, it ramps from -Ipk to +Ipk in that interval, so 2Ipk = 20 A and Ipk = 10.0 A.
